API v1 — Integration Manual

The SATOM exposes a small, versioned, token-authenticated HTTP API at /api/v1 for third-party integrations and automation.

  • Base URL: https://{host}.example.net/api/v1
  • Auth: every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Format: JSON in, JSON out (always — even on errors)

This surface is deliberately narrow. It cannot upgrade, flash or reboot a device, and it cannot run any action flagged destructive — no token, of any scope, can reach those.

In the terms of the NAF Framework (naf-alignment.md) this API is part of Presentation: the door other systems use. What it opens onto is the appliance inventory, health, configuration history, findings and the metrics store (Observability), the pre-created Scheduled Actions, the Processes and the external approval of a Change Request (Orchestrator), and the object authoring below — WAF carve-outs, FortiADC rules, templates, bindings and baselines (Intent). The OpenAPI document (§10) describes every route of this surface.

There are exactly three ways to change anything, and they are not interchangeable:

  1. Scheduled Actions (§3) — operational moves an operator pre-created for you. You trigger one by id; you cannot alter the parameters it was saved with.
  2. Object authoring (§6 FortiWeb, §7 FortiADC) — you write your own WAF carve-out or FortiADC rule. Only a type on a curated allow-list, and only if an administrator granted your token the matching capability.
  3. Intent (§12) — templates, bindings and baselines: desired state. Only with the template_draft / template_apply capabilities, and a push to a device is the console's own canary-gated job, never a direct write.

The same page also exposes what SATOM has recorded — configuration history and diffs, findings, metrics (§13) — and describes itself as an OpenAPI document (§10).

Object authoring is not a proxy to the appliance configuration database. No token, of any scope, can author an administrator account, an interface or a route through this API: those types are not on the list, and the list is published by the API itself (GET /waf/exception-types, GET /adc/rule-types).

1. Getting a token

Tokens are issued by an administrator in the app (API Tokens section). You cannot self-serve one from this page — ask an admin. When a token is created you receive the plaintext once; it is stored only as a hash and can never be shown again. A token looks like:

fmk_<public_id>_<secret>

Each token has four chained limits you should understand before you rely on it. All four are evaluated on every call; the first that says no wins:

Limit Meaning
Scope read ⊂ write ⊂ admin. Triggering an action needs write.
Owner-capped The token never exceeds its owner's role. If the owner lacks config_write, the token's write scope does nothing. Disable the owner → the token dies with them.
Product (ADOM) The token is bound to fortiweb, fortiadc or global and acts only on that product.
Capability Object authoring (§6, §7) is refused unless the token carries the matching capability — waf_exception_draft / waf_exception_apply / adc_rule_draft / adc_rule_apply. An empty capability list means no object writes at all; it is never read as "everything". Ask the administrator for the one you need, by name.

A write token with an empty capability list is not scoped to a single action or device: it can run every non-destructive catalog action enabled in its ADOM that needs no explicit grant. Treat it as a credential for all of that automation, or ask for a token restricted to named capabilities (below).

Draft and apply are different credentials, not a flag you choose. A token holding only *_draft that sends "apply": true is refused with 403 capability_denied and nothing is written — it is never quietly downgraded to a draft. That matters: a silent downgrade would return success to an automation that then believes the hole is closed.

2. Authentication

Send the token on every call as a Bearer header:

Authorization: Bearer fmk_abc123_def456...

Missing/blank → 401 unauthenticated. Wrong/expired/revoked → 401 invalid_token. The API never issues an HTML login redirect — you always get JSON.

3. Endpoints

Paths are relative to the base URL. Scope is the minimum token scope; capability is the extra explicit grant, where one applies.

Method Path Scope Capability Purpose
GET /ping read — Identity of the token (owner, scopes, product)
GET /appliances read — Device inventory + cached status
GET /appliances/<id> read — One device
POST /appliances/<id>/firmware-check write inventory Ask the device its running firmware, live (§8)
GET /actions read — Scheduled actions visible to the token
POST /actions/<id>/run write — Trigger a non-destructive action
GET /actions/runs/<run_id> read — Poll the outcome of a run
POST /change-requests/<id>/external-approval admin — Record the external change authority's verdict on a change request in External approval mode (below)
GET /waf/exception-types read — The allow-list of WAF carve-out types (§6)
GET /waf/exceptions read — Carve-outs this token authored (?all=1 needs admin)
GET /waf/exceptions/<id> read — One carve-out
POST /waf/exceptions write waf_exception_draft (+ waf_exception_apply for "apply": true) File a WAF carve-out (§6)
DELETE /waf/exceptions/<id> write waf_exception_draft Withdraw one you authored, from desired state only (§6)
GET /adc/rule-types read — The allow-list of FortiADC rule types (§7)
GET /adc/rules read — FortiADC rules of a type, read from the appliance (§7)
POST /adc/rules write adc_rule_draft (+ adc_rule_apply for "apply": true) Create a FortiADC rule (§7)
GET /ui/themes read — The theme names on this node and which one is active (§8)
GET /ui/theme read — One theme as a satom.ui-theme/2 document: tokens, logo and favicon; the active theme, or ?name= (§8)
GET /system/nodes read monitoring, only on a capability-restricted token CPU, memory and disk of every SATOM node now, graded (§9). Global token only
GET /system/nodes/history read monitoring, only on a capability-restricted token The same readings over time (§9). Global token only
GET /openapi.json read — This API as an OpenAPI 3.0 document, built from the live routes (§10)
GET /templates read — Templates of the token's ADOM (§11)
GET /templates/<id> read — One template: body, versions, review history, bindings (§11)
GET /bindings read — Template bindings of the ADOM, ?appliance=<id> for one device (§11)
GET /baselines read — Baselines of the token's ADOM (§11)
GET /baselines/<id> read — One baseline with its templates (§11)
POST /templates write template_draft Create a template, or a new version of one (§12)
PUT /templates/<id> write template_draft Save a new version (versions are immutable) (§12)
DELETE /templates/<id> write template_draft Delete an unlocked version (§12)
POST /templates/<id>/approve write template_apply Approve (four-eyes: never the author) (§12)
POST /templates/<id>/reject write template_apply Reject with a reason (§12)
POST /templates/<id>/unapprove write template_apply Revoke an approval (§12)
POST /templates/<id>/apply write template_apply Preview, or start the canary-gated apply job (§12)
POST /bindings write template_draft Bind a device to a template family (§12)
DELETE /bindings/<id> write template_draft Remove a binding (§12)
POST /baselines write template_draft Create a baseline (§12)
PUT /baselines/<id> write template_draft Update a baseline (§12)
DELETE /baselines/<id> write template_draft Delete a baseline (§12)
GET /appliances/<id>/config-history read — Recorded configuration versions of one device (§13)
GET /appliances/<id>/config-diff read — What changed between two versions, ?from=&to= (§13)
GET /findings read monitoring, only on a capability-restricted token What the alert engine finds right now (§13)
GET /metrics/query read monitoring, only on a capability-restricted token A read-only MetricsQL query over SATOM's own series (§13)
GET /processes read — The processes the token's ADOM may see (§14)
GET /processes/<id> read — One process, with its diagram (§14)
POST /processes/<id>/run write process_arm for "armed": true Walk a process — a rehearsal unless armed (§14)
GET /process-runs/<id> read — One walk and its steps; poll a run parked on a manual gate (§14)

The write endpoints are rate-limited to 30/min, like /actions/<id>/run.

GET /ping

Verify a token and see what it can do.

{
  "ok": true,
  "token": "abc123",
  "name": "integration-drain-bot",
  "owner": "svc-external",
  "scopes": ["read", "write"],
  "product": "fortiweb"
}

GET /appliances / GET /appliances/<id>

Returns the devices the token's owner may see. Each device:

{
  "id": 6,
  "name": "{device}",
  "kind": "fortiweb",
  "host": "{ip}",
  "port": 443,
  "status": "up",
  "last_checked_at": "2026-07-08T18:00:00+00:00",
  "maintenance": false,
  "firmware": "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8,build1128(GA.M),260602",
  "firmware_checked_at": "2026-08-13T00:09:43.036612",
  "model": "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8",
  "hw_type": "vm"
}

firmware is verbatim as the vendor spells it — SATOM does not normalise it. Turning that string into a comparable version is a matching rule that belongs to whatever owns the vulnerability dictionary; a second copy of the rule here would drift from it.

firmware_checked_at is the half that makes the version usable. null means nobody ever confirmed this version against the device — it may be an operator's note, or a reading from a firmware ago. A consumer that correlates versions against advisories should refuse an unattested row rather than publish a verdict about a box it never observed.

POST /appliances/<id>/firmware-check

Ask ONE device what it is running, right now. Read-only against the appliance (a single status call, the same one the connectivity probe makes) and it can never reach the firmware upgrade path, which is hard-blocked on this API.

Requires the write scope and the explicit inventory capability: an empty capability list does not grant it. Rate-limited to 10/min — every call opens an authenticated session to a live firewall.

Success (200):

{
  "ok": true,
  "id": 14,
  "name": "{device}",
  "kind": "fortiweb",
  "firmware": "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8,build1128(GA.M),260602",
  "model": "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8",
  "hw_type": "vm",
  "checked_at": "2026-08-13T00:09:43.036612",
  "changed": true,
  "previous": "7.6.8",
  "source": "live"
}

changed: false means the version did not move — it is still a fresh observation, and checked_at advances.

Failure (502) — the device was not reached, or answered without a version:

{
  "error": "device_refused",
  "detail": "errcode -20010: The license of peer VM FortiWeb is not valid.",
  "message": "The appliance did not return a firmware version; nothing was recorded.",
  "firmware": "FortiWeb-KVM 7.6.8,build1128(GA.M),260602",
  "firmware_checked_at": null
}

A failed check writes nothing — not even the timestamp. The last known value and its (possibly null) age are echoed so the caller can decide whether the stale reading is still good enough for it. If firmware_checked_at could be stamped by a check that never reached a device, the field would mean nothing to anyone.

GET /actions

Lists the scheduled actions in the token's ADOM. Look at api_runnable: a destructive action (danger: true) is shown but can never be triggered through the API.

{
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": 42,
      "name": "Drain backend web-01",
      "action": "backend_set_status",
      "label": "Enable/disable a pool member",
      "scope": "user",
      "product": "fortiweb",
      "enabled": true,
      "schedule_kind": "manual",
      "last_run": null,
      "last_status": "",
      "next_run": null,
      "danger": false,
      "api_runnable": true
    }
  ]
}

POST /actions/<id>/run

Triggers the action with the parameters it was saved with. Rate-limited to 30/min. Returns the run id so you can poll it.

Which actions a token may trigger is decided by its capabilities (the administrator ticks them when minting the token). Each catalog action belongs to one capability:

capability actions empty list grants it?
backend_edit / backend_config / policy_status / cert_swap backend_set_status / backend_set_config / policy_set_status / swap_certificate (AppID-scopable) yes
maintenance backup, device_sync, device_inspect, deep_capture, signature_sync, system_backup, cert_scan, appid_import yes
reports stats, inventory_snapshot, health_check, ha_check yes
cert_renew cert_manager_server, cert_manager_clientserver, cert_manager_client no
monitoring deep_monitor, metrics_scrape, monitor_report no
sentinel sentinel_sweep, sentinel_baseline, sentinel_vuln_sync, sentinel_feed_publish no
feeds signature_check, knowledge_fetch, artifact_refs no
api_library apilib_harvest, schema_harvest, schema_watch no
netbox netbox_reconcile no

A token with a non-empty list runs only the actions of the capabilities it lists. The capabilities marked no were added on 2026-10-15: before that those actions had no capability, and only a token owned by a user administrator could run them. An empty list keeps that rule for them, so no token issued earlier gained anything. Destructive actions (upgrade, upgrade_prep, reboot, ha_failover, cert_lifecycle, custom_rest) are never runnable through the API, whatever the token holds. System Automations also need an owner with user management rights.

{
  "ok": true,
  "run_id": 99,
  "action_id": 42,
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "disable backend web-01 on pool pool-web"
}

GET /actions/runs/<run_id>

Poll a run's outcome.

{
  "run_id": 99,
  "action_id": 42,
  "status": "ok",
  "trigger": "api",
  "summary": "disable backend web-01 on pool pool-web",
  "started_at": "2026-07-08T18:01:00+00:00",
  "finished_at": "2026-07-08T18:01:04+00:00"
}

POST /change-requests/<id>/external-approval

The external change authority's verdict on a change request whose approval mode is External. Needs the admin scope (owner holds user_manage). Body: {"approved": true|false, "by": "CAB", "detail": "CHG-7"} — approved is required and must be a JSON boolean; by (default: the token name) is recorded as api:<by>. false withdraws an earlier approval, which makes the change un-runnable again.

answer when
200 {"ok": true, "external_approved_at": …} recorded
400 bad_request approved missing or not a boolean
404 not_found no such change, or it names no appliance visible to the token's ADOM
409 not_external / 409 closed the change is approved in SATOM (Manual mode), or already completed / failed / cancelled — nothing recorded

Every call is audited (api.change_request.external_approval, refusals as …_refused).

4. A complete example — drain / restore a backend

The API cannot re-point a backend to a new IP; what it can do is enable / disable a pool member (drain or restore it). The recipe:

  1. An admin creates a dedicated user (role operator, so it has config_write).
  2. In Automation → Scheduled Actions, pre-create two actions and note their ids: - backend_set_status with enabled=false → "drain backend X" - backend_set_status with enabled=true → "restore backend X"
  3. The admin issues a token: owner = that user, product = fortiweb, scope = write.

Then the integrator calls:

TOKEN="fmk_abc123_def456..."
BASE="https://{host}.example.net/api/v1"

# 1. Verify the token
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/ping | jq

# 2. Find the action id (api_runnable:true)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/actions \
  | jq '.actions[] | {id, name, action, api_runnable}'

# 3. Drain the backend (action id 42)
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/actions/42/run | jq
#  -> {"ok":true,"run_id":99,"status":"ok","summary":"disable backend ..."}

# 4. Poll the result
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $BASE/actions/runs/99 | jq

5. Errors

Every error is JSON with an error code (and usually a message).

HTTP error When
401 unauthenticated No / malformed Authorization header
401 invalid_token Unknown, expired or revoked token
403 insufficient_scope Token scope too low for the endpoint
403 owner_forbidden / owner_disabled Owner lacks the permission, or is disabled
403 wrong_product Token's ADOM cannot touch that action's product
403 destructive_blocked Firmware upgrade/flash/reboot — never allowed via API
404 not_found No such action / run (or not visible to this token)
409 disabled The action — or the process — is disabled
409 already_running The action is already running
403 capability_denied "armed": true on a process walk without the process_arm capability (§14)
400 appliance_required / invalid_diagram A process walk needs a device, or its diagram cannot run yet (§14)
429 rate_limited Too many requests (run is 30/min)

Object authoring answers with these too, plus its own set — see §7 → Additional error codes for the full list.

Every authenticated call and every run is audited (who, when, which token), and so is every refusal of an object write: the denial reason is recorded against your token.

6. WAF carve-outs — /api/v1/waf/* (FortiWeb)

File an exception on the Web Protection Profile in front of your application.

This is not a proxy to the FortiWeb configuration database. The type you may author comes from a curated catalog, and only the exception half of it — signature customisations edit a shared signature set and stay operator-only. GET /waf/exception-types publishes the exact allow-list, with the required fields and the enum values for each type; it is the same list the server enforces.

Two capabilities decide what your token may do. They are granted by an administrator on the token and cannot be requested in the call:

capability effect
waf_exception_draft Records the carve-out as desired state and returns the exact device request that would be sent. Never touches an appliance.
waf_exception_apply May additionally push it, with "apply": true.

A draft-only token that sends "apply": true gets 403 capability_denied and nothing is written — it is never silently downgraded to a draft.

# 1. What may I author?
curl -sH "$AUTH" https://satom/api/v1/waf/exception-types | jq '.types[].key'

# 2. File one (draft — no device is touched)
curl -sX POST -H "$AUTH" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://satom/api/v1/waf/exceptions -d '{
    "appliance_id": 3,
    "wpp_mkey": "wpp-app1",
    "exc_type": "allow_method_exception_item",
    "policies": ["pol-app1"],
    "reason": "CVE-2026-1234 mitigation needs PATCH on /api/v2/upload",
    "payload": {"request-type": "plain",
                "request-file": "/api/v2/upload",
                "allow-request": "put patch"}
  }'
# -> 201 {"created":true,"applied":false,"exception":{...},"plan":{...}}

# 3. With an apply-capable token, push it (target = the device object it goes in)
#    ... same body plus:  "target": "am-exc", "apply": true

GET /waf/exceptions?appliance_id=3 lists the carve-outs your token authored. ?all=1 widens to every carve-out on the appliance and needs the admin scope. DELETE /waf/exceptions/<id> withdraws one you authored — from desired state only: if it was already applied, the entry is still on the appliance and the response says so.

AppID-scoped tokens. If your token is pinned to AppIDs you must list the policies the carve-out is for, and they must be yours. You will also be refused when the Web Protection Profile you named is bound to a policy outside your scope: a profile is usually shared, so the exception would apply to every application on it. Ask an operator for a dedicated profile (clone + rebind).

7. FortiADC rules — /api/v1/adc/*

Same capability model (adc_rule_draft / adc_rule_apply), same curated allow-list (GET /adc/rule-types), one honest difference: FortiADC writes go straight to the appliance because there is no desired-state store for it. So:

  • "apply": false (the default) returns the exact request that would be sent, built locally — no session is opened.
  • Creating a name that already exists is refused with 409 already_exists rather than risking an overwrite of an object your token does not own.
  • An applied create is read back from the appliance. The 201 answer carries verify: verified (the appliance holds the object with the fields you sent), or unverified with the reason (only secrets were sent, the re-read failed). An appliance that accepted the POST and does not hold the object answers 502 not_applied, with verify.mismatch naming each field the appliance holds differently.
  • There is no DELETE. Without a store there is no recorded author, so "delete only what you created" cannot be proven, and an endpoint that cannot tell your object from an operator's is a way to remove someone else's protection. Withdrawal is an operator action.
  • An AppID-scoped token cannot use this surface at all: AppID scope resolves to FortiWeb server policies and is unprovable here.

Additional error codes

HTTP error When
400 bad_request The body is not a JSON object
400 type_not_allowed The carve-out type / ADC logical is not on the allow-list
400 invalid_payload Required fields missing or badly formatted (errors[] says which)
400 target_required apply: true without the device object to write into
403 capability_denied The token lacks *_draft / *_apply
403 appid_scope_unresolved An AppID-scoped token did not name its policies
403 appid_scope_denied A named policy is outside the token's AppID scope
403 wpp_shared_denied The profile is bound to a policy outside the scope
403 wpp_scope_unprovable SATOM cannot prove the profile is unshared (no cache)
403 not_appid_scopable An AppID-scoped token on the FortiADC surface
409 template_locked The profile is template-managed; templates stay clean
409 already_exists An ADC object of that name is already on the appliance
500 registry_mismatch The rule type resolved to an endpoint SATOM cannot address — report it; retrying will not help
502 device_unreachable SATOM could not open a session to the appliance
502 device_error The appliance rejected or could not serve the write
502 not_applied The appliance accepted the write, but reading it back shows it does not hold it (verify says what differs)

This manual is hand-written, and that is exactly why it is pinned by a test. tests/test_api_v1_manual.py fails when a route, an object-write capability or an error code exists in the code and not in this page — a manual that quietly loses an endpoint looks identical to one that is complete, and a reader who cannot find a capability concludes the product does not have it.*

8. Sharing the console theme — /api/v1/ui/*

Another SATOM node calls GET /ui/theme when an admin uses Settings → Appearance → Import from a site… → Another SATOM node. Mint a read token on the node that HAS the theme and paste it on the node that wants it; the token is used for that one request and is not stored there.

  • GET /ui/theme returns the active theme; GET /ui/theme?name=<theme name> any other one (404 not_found if no theme has that name).
  • The answer is the same document Export downloads (schema satom.ui-theme/2): name, description, tokens (overrides only) and assets.logo / assets.favicon as {"type": "png"|"svg", "data": <base64>}. The receiving node validates it exactly like an imported file: one bad token or an asset that is not an image refuses the whole document.
  • read is enough on purpose: a theme is colours plus the logo the sign-in page already shows to anyone, and nothing on this surface writes.
  • Rate-limited to 30/min.

9. SATOM node resources — /api/v1/system/*

CPU, memory and disk of the SATOM nodes themselves (not of the appliances): the readings behind Monitoring → SATOM health and its Resource history charts, for an outside monitoring system.

Access. A read token bound to the global ADOM. A token bound to a product gets 403 wrong_product, because SATOM health is Global-only and the API gives no more than a session gets. A token restricted to named capabilities also needs monitoring (403 capability_denied otherwise). An empty capability list is enough, as for every other GET. Rate-limited to 60/min. Node addresses are never in the answer.

GET /system/nodes

Every node as it is now, graded against Settings → Thresholds (SATOM machine):

{"status": "ok",
 "limits": {"disk_warn_pct": 80, "disk_crit_pct": 92, "mem_warn_pct": 80, ...},
 "nodes": [
  {"name": "{primary-node}", "role": "primary", "is_local": true,
   "reachable": true, "status": "ok", "reasons": [],
   "cpus": 4, "cpu_pct": 1.7,
   "mem_total_mb": 4096, "mem_used_mb": 1309, "mem_pct": 32.0,
   "disks": [{"mount": "/", "total_gb": 26.2, "used_gb": 20.4, "pct": 77.8}],
   "uptime_s": 824592},
  {"name": "{standby-node}", "role": null, "reachable": false,
   "status": "unknown", "cpu_pct": null, ...}]}

A node that did not answer is reachable: false, status: "unknown", and its readings are null. Its last known numbers are not repeated.

GET /system/nodes/history

Parameter Values Default
range 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d 24h
node a node name ({primary-node}) every node
metrics comma-separated: cpu, mem, disk (percent), mem_used_mb, mem_total_mb, disk_used_gb, disk_total_gb, up (1 answered, 0 did not) cpu,mem,disk 
{"ok": true, "range": "24h", "start": 1792454700, "end": 1792541100,
 "step_s": 240, "errors": [],
 "series": [
  {"key": "cpu", "metric": "satom_node_cpu_pct", "unit": "%",
   "node": "{primary-node}", "mount": null,
   "points": [[1792454700, 2.1], [1792454940, 1.8], ...]},
  {"key": "disk", "metric": "satom_node_disk_pct", "unit": "%",
   "node": "{primary-node}", "mount": "/", "points": [...]}]}
  • points are [unix seconds, value], one per step_s, at most 400 per series. Each is the highest reading in its step, so a peak is not averaged away on long ranges. Steps are never finer than the 3-minute sample cadence.
  • A missing point is a gap: no sample in the step plus the six minutes before it (the node did not answer, or the action did not run). It is never filled in.
  • Samples are written by the metrics_scrape scheduled action. A node only has history from the release that added these series onward.
  • If the metrics store does not answer, the response is 502 store_unavailable, with the store's message under errors. It is never a 200 with empty series, which a poller would record as "no load".
  • A bad range, node or metrics is 400 bad_request.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://{host}.example.net/api/v1/system/nodes/history?range=7d&metrics=disk_used_gb"

10. The API as a document — GET /openapi.json

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://{host}.example.net/api/v1/openapi.json

An OpenAPI 3.0 document of every path and method this API serves, built at request time from the live routes: the scope each view enforces (x-satom-scope), the explicit capabilities it asks for (x-satom-capabilities), its path parameters and its documented responses. It is not written by hand and it is not generated into a file at release time, so it cannot lag behind the code: a route is in the document the moment it is registered. Feed it to a client generator or a request explorer; this page remains the prose explanation of why each gate exists.

The security scheme is bearerAuth (HTTP bearer). Scope and capabilities are vendor extensions because OpenAPI's own security scopes describe OAuth, not SATOM's owner-capped ladder.

11. Intent, read — /api/v1/templates, /bindings, /baselines

In the vocabulary of the NAF Framework this is the Intent block: the desired state SATOM keeps as Templates (versioned, reviewed bodies), Template bindings (which device a template family governs, with its per-device values) and Baselines (a scoped assembly of approved templates). Reading needs the read scope and an owner who may open the Templates page (operations.view, else 403 owner_forbidden). Everything is scoped to the token's ADOM exactly like a console session of that ADOM: another product's template or baseline is 404 not_found, never a 403.

GET /templates

Newest version first. Filters: ?kind=, ?status=pending|approved|rejected (anything else is 400 bad_request), ?name=. Rows carry identity, status, author, provenance and the build they were written for — not the body.

GET /templates/<id>

The template with its body, exceptions, validated_builds, every versions[] of its family (id, version, status, author, created_at), the review_history[] (who approved, rejected or revoked, when, why) and its bindings[].

GET /bindings

Bindings of every device the token may see; ?appliance=<id> narrows to one device (404 when it is not in the ADOM). Each: appliance_id, kind, name, pinned_version (null = follow the newest approved version), variables, note, created_by.

GET /baselines / GET /baselines/<id>

The baselines of the ADOM with their scope (zone, line, department); the detail lists the templates[] that compose it (id, kind, name, version, section, position).

12. Intent, write — templates, bindings and baselines

Two explicit-only capabilities, in the same model as §6: an empty capability list authorises none of this, and the caller never picks its own privilege.

Capability What it allows
template_draft Create a template or a new version of one, delete an unlocked version, bind or unbind a device, author baselines. Never touches an appliance. The owner must hold operations.template_save.
template_apply Approve, reject or revoke a template (owner must hold operations.template_approve, an administrator permission) and push a template to devices (owner must hold operations.template_apply).

A token bound to one product may hold them for that product only; a global token for every product. Every call is audited with the token's public id, and the records it creates carry api:<public_id> as author or reviewer. The write endpoints are rate-limited to 30/min; apply to 10/min.

POST /templates

{"kind": "web-protection-profile", "name": "api-wpp", "body": {...},
 "note": "", "exceptions": null, "source_firmware": "7.6.8"}

Creates a pending draft of the token's ADOM (201), or — when the kind/name already exists — the next version of that family. body must be a JSON object; an unknown kind, a missing name or an unknown build is 400 bad_request. source_firmware is optional: it records the build the body was written for, which is what lets a later build be compared against it.

PUT /templates/<id>

Versions are immutable, as in the console: this saves a new version of the same family (body, note, exceptions; fields absent keep the predecessor's), pending, with the predecessor's build stamp. The answer is the new version.

DELETE /templates/<id>

Deletes one version. A locked (curated) template is 409 locked.

POST /templates/<id>/approve · /reject · /unapprove

The review lifecycle. Approval is the four-eyes rule of the console: the token that authored the template may not approve it (409 review_refused). reject takes {"reason": "..."}. Every verdict lands in the template's review history with the token as reviewer.

POST /templates/<id>/apply

{"appliance_ids": [12, 13], "confirm": false, "override_reason": ""}

This is the console's own path and nothing else:

  • Without confirm (or with anything but the boolean true): a preview — the per-device plan, the firmware-compatibility verdicts and any unresolved {{ variable }} — and no device is contacted for real.
  • With confirm: true: the same gates run (unresolved variables and a refused firmware check are 409 apply_refused, with the console's compat report), then the apply starts as the background job the console starts: canary device first, the rest only if the canary succeeds. The answer is 202 {"mode": "apply", "job_id": ...}; the job's progress and its completion audit row are the console's. override_reason is honoured only for an owner holding operations.template_approve, exactly like the console's override.
  • More than one device is a fleet rollout: the template must be approved (409 apply_refused) and the owner must hold operations.apply (403 owner_forbidden).
  • An appliance outside the token's ADOM is 404 not_found for the whole call.

There is no endpoint that writes a template to a device directly, and apply never bypasses the dry-run → canary order.

POST /bindings · DELETE /bindings/<id>

{"template_id": 7, "appliance_id": 12, "pinned_version": null,
 "variables": {"hostname": "app.example"}, "note": ""}

Creates or updates the binding of a device to the template's family. Desired state only: nothing is pushed. A device of another product (400 bad_request: a FortiWeb template cannot govern a FortiADC) or a pinned version that does not exist is refused. Deleting a binding leaves the device as it is.

POST /baselines · PUT /baselines/<id> · DELETE /baselines/<id>

{"name": "zone-a", "zone": "A", "line": "", "department": "",
 "template_ids": [7, 9], "note": ""}

Only approved templates of the token's ADOM can compose a baseline (400 bad_request otherwise). PUT changes the fields present and keeps the others. Deleting a baseline leaves its templates untouched.

Additional error codes

HTTP error When
403 owner_forbidden The owner lacks the permission the call needs (operations.view, operations.template_save, operations.template_approve, operations.template_apply, operations.apply)
409 locked The template is locked (curated) and cannot be deleted
409 review_refused The authoring token tried to approve its own template
409 apply_refused Unresolved variables, an unapproved template for a fleet rollout, or the firmware-compatibility gate refused

13. Observability — configuration history, findings, metrics

In the vocabulary of the NAF Framework this is the Observability block: what SATOM has recorded about the estate. SATOM calls the configuration history its Source of Truth; it is the history of the actual state of every device. Everything here is read-only and needs the read scope.

GET /appliances/<id>/config-history

The recorded configuration versions of one device, newest first (?limit=, default 30, at most 200). A version is identified by its sha256: an unchanged configuration records no new version, so the list is the list of changes. Each row: id, sha256, taken_at, last_seen_at, size_raw, size_gz, total_objects, section_count, source, and whether the payload was evacuated to the backup server. Device secrets were stripped when the version was recorded.

GET /appliances/<id>/config-diff?from=<ref>&to=<ref>

What changed between two versions of the same device (from and to are version ids or sha256 hashes from config-history; a version of another device is 404 not_found). The answer lists added[], removed[] and changed[] object paths (section/endpoint/key), changed_detail[] with per-field before/after for the first changed objects, identical, and truncated when the lists were capped. A version whose payload is no longer available is 410 blob_missing.

GET /findings

What the alert engine finds right now: every enabled check is evaluated on the call (the same evaluation as Settings → Alerts → Preview), so the call costs a check cycle and is rate-limited to 6/min. Each finding: key, family, severity (critical / warning / info), title, detail and, for a device finding, product. A token bound to a product receives that product's findings only; the installation's own (certificates, host, backups, code) need a global token. A token restricted to named capabilities must hold monitoring (403 capability_denied).

GET /metrics/query?expr=…

A read-only MetricsQL query over SATOM's metrics store. Instant query by default; a range query with start and end (unix seconds, at most 90 days apart) and step (60s, 5m, 1h…; default 60s). The answer is the store's own (status, data.resultType, data.result).

  • Only SATOM's own series (satom_*) may be read. An expression naming any other series is 400 bad_request and never reaches the store; so is an expression that names no series at all.
  • The store answers within 10 s or the call is 504 store_timeout; a store error is 502 store_unavailable. Never an empty 200.
  • A token bound to a product receives only the series labelled with its own devices (device / kind); the SATOM nodes' own readings and other products' devices are filtered out of the answer. A global token receives everything.
  • The store itself stays on loopback with no account of its own; this route is the only way in from outside. A token restricted to named capabilities must hold monitoring.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --get \
  --data-urlencode 'expr=max by (device) (satom_box_cpu_pct)' \
  https://{host}.example.net/api/v1/metrics/query

Additional error codes

HTTP error When
410 blob_missing A version's payload is no longer available (pruned and not on the backup server)
502 store_unavailable The metrics store answered an error
504 store_timeout The metrics store did not answer within 10 s

14. Processes — /api/v1/processes/*

Walk a Process (Administrator → Process: a diagram of checks, gates and actions SATOM walks and judges) from outside, and read what a walk did. This is the NAF Orchestrator's "startable by a machine" door, and it is as narrow as the Run button.

Access. read lists and reads; write walks. The token's ADOM sees exactly the processes the console would show it (a process is offered per ADOM; a global token sees every one, drafts included). A walk from the API is a rehearsal by default: every write step dry-runs and the run says so. "armed": true additionally needs the explicit process_arm capability on the token — tokens minted before this surface existed can rehearse and cannot write. Rate-limited to 30/min like the other write endpoints.

GET /processes / GET /processes/<id>

{"processes": [
  {"id": 3, "key": "dr-failover-check", "name": "DR failover check",
   "products": ["fortiweb"], "enabled": true,
   "needs_appliance": true, "writes": true, "steps": 7,
   "trigger_event": "alert.fired",
   "trigger_filter": {"families": ["device"], "min_severity": "critical"},
   "armed_on_trigger": false, "trigger_rate_limit": 10,
   "updated_at": "2026-10-21T02:10:00"}]}

GET /processes/<id> adds "graph" (the nodes and arrows, as the editor stores them).

POST /processes/<id>/run

Body: {"appliance_id": 7, "armed": false} — both optional. appliance_id is required when needs_appliance is true (400 appliance_required). The walk runs inline and the answer is the finished run (or the run parked on a manual gate — status: "waiting", waiting_node), with its steps:

{"id": 41, "process_key": "dr-failover-check", "appliance": "fw-dmz-02",
 "armed": false, "status": "done", "verdict": "ok",
 "summary": "5 step(s) ran and every one of them passed.",
 "trigger": "api", "trigger_key": "api-token:1f3a…", "started_by": "svc-noc",
 "counts": {"pass": 5, "fail": 0, "unknown": 0, "skipped": 0},
 "steps": [{"seq": 1, "key": "start", "kind": "start", "status": "pass",
            "detail": "process entered", "dry_run": false, "undo_recorded": false}, …]}

Arming a diagram that only reads is dropped silently, as on the Run button. A disabled process answers 409 disabled; a diagram the editor would refuse to run answers 400 invalid_diagram with the problems listed.

GET /process-runs/<id>

The same document, for polling. A run whose process has been deleted is shown to a global token only — the console applies the same rule.

# rehearse, then arm once the rehearsal is clean
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"appliance_id": 7}' https://satom.example.com/api/v1/processes/3/run
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"appliance_id": 7, "armed": true}' https://satom.example.com/api/v1/processes/3/run
#  -> 403 capability_denied unless the token holds process_arm
